question: For a normalized general scalar harmonic Q_I on the unit round S3 with Delta Q_I=-lambda Q_I and lambda=n(n+2), do integration by parts and the Bochner identity fix the normalized scalar-derived vector and tracefree tensor harmonics, their divergence identities, and the n=0/1 degeneracies exactly?

upstream_results.role: pins the unit-S3 geometry, curvature convention, and the fact that its ADM result is a convention baseline rather than HDA evidence

primary_sources.source: J. J. Halliwell and S. W. Hawking, Origin of Structure in the Universe, Phys. Rev. D 31 (1985) 1777
primary_sources.used_for: closed-universe scalar/vector/tensor harmonic context and low-mode caution

declared_conventions.geometry: unit round S3 with Ric_ab=2 gamma_ab, scalar curvature 6, and compact boundaryless integration by parts
declared_conventions.scalar_harmonic: integral_S3 sqrt(gamma) Q_I Q_J=delta_IJ and Delta Q_I=-lambda_n Q_I, lambda_n=n(n+2)
declared_conventions.divergence_sign: D^a V_a=-sqrt(lambda_n) Q_I and D^b T_ab=-sqrt((2/3)*(lambda_n-3)) V_a
declared_conventions.low_mode_policy: n=0 has no normalized gradient vector; n=1 has a normalized gradient vector but zero tracefree-Hessian tensor; tensor normalization starts at n=2

exact_plan: hash-verify the committed ADM convention result and preserve its non-HDA scope
use integration by parts to verify integral |DQ|^2=lambda
use the integrated Bochner identity with Ric_ab=2 gamma_ab to verify integral |D_aD_b Q|^2=lambda(lambda-2)
derive the tracefree-Hessian norm (2/3)lambda(lambda-3) and divergence identity
verify normalized scalar-derived vector and tensor norms and divergences algebraically
evaluate n=0 through four to expose the n=0 vector and n=1 tensor degeneracies
leave complete SVT harmonics, Gaunt/Clebsch-Gordan data, ADM constraints, cubic expansion, HDA/Jacobi, BFV and all physical outputs null
